message.content:
Below is a ready‑to‑run **gcloud** command (the official CLI for Google Cloud) that creates a Compute Engine VM with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
If you prefer the raw REST‑API payload, I’ve also supplied a minimal JSON body that can be sent to the `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` endpoint.

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI Command

```bash
# Replace PROJECT_ID and ZONE with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust if needed
    --subnet=default \
    --network-tier=PREMIUM \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --provisioning-model=STANDARD \
    --service-account=default@${PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --boot-disk-device-name=rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --no-shielded-secure-boot \
    --no-shielded-vtpm \
    --no-shielded-integrity-monitoring \
    --guest-accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000 \
    --reservation-affinity=any \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: custom init script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM allocation (`n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM). |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS base image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Persistent Disk size/type. |
| `--guest-accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional shell script that runs at boot (e.g., installs drivers). |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs or a different machine family, change `count=` and `type=` accordingly. For example, `count=2,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000` for two GPUs.

---

## 2️⃣ REST API Payload (JSON)

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default@my-gcp-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> **How to use it:**  
> 1. Replace `"my-gcp-project"` and `"us-central1-a"` with your project ID and zone.  
> 2. Send a POST request to `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<project>/zones/<zone>/instances`.  
> 3. Include an OAuth 2.0 bearer token with scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute`.

---

## 3️⃣ Quick Startup Script (Optional)

If you want the instance to automatically install the NVIDIA driver after boot, create a file named `startup.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
apt-get update
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
```

Then reference it in the gcloud command with `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh`.

---

### Final Checklist

- [ ] Verify you have the **Compute Engine API** enabled in your project.  
- [ ] Ensure you have sufficient quota for **GPU** usage in the selected zone.  
- [ ] Run the gcloud command or POST the JSON payload.  
- [ ] After creation, SSH into the instance and run `nvidia-smi` to confirm the GPU is visible.

Happy computing!
